item.title: Licensing and Attribution
item.description:
This checklist helps maintainers keep MATE releases compliant with license obligations across all repositories.

Why this matters

MATE is a multi-repository, volunteer-driven project. License mistakes in one component can affect downstream distributions and users, so we handle licensing as a shared responsibility.

Checklist for merge requests and releases

  1. Verify new files include the correct license header used by that repository.
  2. Verify copied or imported code keeps upstream copyright and license notices.
  3. Confirm third-party code additions include a clear source reference in commit messages or PR notes.
  4. Ensure bundled assets (icons, images, themes, docs) have redistribution rights compatible with the repository license.
  5. Update any license manifest files used by the project (for example COPYING, LICENSE, or equivalent notice files).
  6. If license compatibility is unclear, pause merge and ask for maintainer review in the PR.

Third-party dependency expectations

  • Prefer dependencies already packaged by major distributions.
  • Prefer licenses compatible with GPL/LGPL project components.
  • Avoid dependencies with unclear ownership, unclear terms, or non-commercial restrictions.

Minimum PR note for external code

When a PR adds external code, include this in the description:

Source: <upstream URL>
License: <license name>
Changes made: <short summary>
Attribution retained: yes/no

Disagreement handling

If maintainers disagree on licensing risk, do not merge immediately. Ask for at least one more maintainer review and document the final decision in the PR thread.

item.title: Consensus and Change Control
item.description:
MATE is maintained by volunteers across time zones without a single project lead. This page defines a practical decision process so important changes stay transparent and reviewable.

When consensus is required

Use consensus review (not unilateral merge) for:

  • Release version bumps and release tags
  • ABI/API changes that affect downstreams
  • Dependency additions or removals
  • Build system migrations and CI policy changes
  • Governance, moderation, or policy documentation changes

Baseline decision rule

  1. Open a PR with clear rationale and impact.
  2. Request review from active maintainers in affected repositories.
  3. Wait for at least one approval for routine changes, or two approvals for high-impact changes.
  4. If concerns remain unresolved, do not merge.

How to resolve disagreement

  • Summarize options in the PR thread.
  • Prefer the option with lowest risk to users and packagers.
  • If no agreement emerges, defer to a maintenance release cycle and revisit with more testing.

Emergency exceptions

Urgent security fixes may be merged faster, but must still be announced to maintainers with follow-up review after merge.

Documentation requirement

For impactful decisions, leave a concise final comment in the PR describing:

  • What was decided
  • Why
  • Any follow-up work

This gives future maintainers an auditable project history.
